entries.name: Chronometer
entries.definition: A precise timekeeping instrument, originally built to keep accurate time at sea so that longitude could be found.

entries.name: Circular economy
entries.definition: An economic approach that keeps products and materials in use as long as possible through reuse, repair, remanufacturing and recycling, so that waste is designed out.

entries.name: Circulatory system
entries.definition: The organ system, made up of the heart, blood vessels and blood, that carries oxygen, nutrients and waste around the body.

entries.name: Cisco Intersight
entries.definition: Cisco's cloud-based platform for managing and monitoring Cisco UCS servers and other data-centre infrastructure from one place.

entries.name: Cisco UCS Director
entries.definition: Cisco software for automating the provisioning and management of compute, network and storage resources in data centres built on Cisco UCS.

entries.name: Civil engineering design
entries.definition: Planning and specifying infrastructure and structures such as roads, bridges, drainage and water systems so that they meet engineering requirements.

entries.name: CKEditor
entries.definition: A JavaScript rich-text editor that lets users format content in web pages.

entries.name: Claim processing
entries.definition: Receiving, checking and deciding insurance or benefit claims, and then paying or denying them.

entries.name: Claims modeling
entries.definition: Building statistical models of how often insurance claims occur and how large they are, to price risk and set reserves.

entries.name: Clarizen
entries.definition: A cloud-based work and project management platform for planning projects, tracking tasks and managing resources.

entries.name: Clash detection
entries.definition: Checking a combined 3D model of a building or plant for places where parts from different disciplines, such as pipes and beams, occupy the same space.

entries.name: Classification and Regression Tree
entries.definition: A decision-tree method that repeatedly splits data into groups to predict either a category (classification) or a number (regression).

entries.name: Clean Air Act
entries.definition: The United States federal law that limits air pollution and gives the Environmental Protection Agency power to set and enforce air quality and emission standards.

entries.name: Clean Water Act
entries.definition: The United States federal law that regulates the discharge of pollutants into US waters and sets water quality standards for surface waters.

entries.name: ClearDB
entries.definition: A managed cloud database service that provides replicated MySQL databases, commonly used as an add-on on platforms such as Heroku.

entries.name: Client access license
entries.definition: A licensing model used by server software, notably from Microsoft, in which each user or device needs a licence to connect to the server.

entries.name: Client confidentiality
entries.definition: Keeping information that clients share private and disclosing it only with their consent or as the law requires.

entries.name: Climate variability and change
entries.definition: The study of natural variation in climate over time and of long-term shifts in it, with their causes and impacts.

entries.name: Clinical data repository
entries.definition: A database that gathers patient data from several clinical systems in one place so that it can be viewed, reported on and reused.

entries.name: Clinical documentation improvement
entries.definition: Reviewing and clarifying patient records so that they accurately and completely describe a patient's condition and care, for coding, billing and quality reporting.

entries.name: Clinical informatics
entries.definition: The use of information science and computing to improve patient care and clinical workflows in health-care settings.

entries.name: Clinical laboratory phlebotomy
entries.definition: Drawing blood from patients, in a clinical laboratory or collection site, for laboratory testing.

entries.name: Clinical medical ethics
entries.definition: Applying ethical principles to decisions in patient care, such as consent, confidentiality and end-of-life treatment.

entries.name: Clinical pastoral education
entries.definition: A programme of supervised, hands-on training in spiritual care for chaplains and ministers, accredited in the United States by the Association for Clinical Pastoral Education.

entries.name: Closed-circuit television camera
entries.definition: A video camera whose signal goes to a limited set of monitors or recorders rather than being broadcast openly, typically used for security and surveillance.

entries.name: Cloud access security broker
entries.definition: Security software or a service placed between an organisation's users and its cloud services to enforce security policies such as visibility, data protection and threat detection.

entries.name: Cloud computing
entries.definition: Designing and using remotely provisioned computing services.

entries.name: Cloud computing security
entries.definition: Protecting the data, applications and infrastructure that run in cloud computing environments.

entries.name: Cloud-native development
entries.definition: Building applications designed to run in the cloud, typically as containerised microservices managed by automated platforms such as Kubernetes.

entries.name: CNC programming
entries.definition: Writing the instructions, often in G-code, that direct computer numerically controlled machine tools to cut or shape parts.

entries.name: Coastal engineering
entries.definition: The branch of civil engineering that designs and manages structures and measures at the shoreline, such as sea walls, harbours and erosion protection.

entries.name: Cocoa Touch
entries.definition: Apple's set of application frameworks, including UIKit, for building apps for iPhone, iPad and other iOS-family devices.

entries.name: CocoaPods
entries.definition: A dependency manager for Swift and Objective-C projects that downloads and links third-party libraries.

entries.name: CocoonJS
entries.definition: A tool from Ludei that packages HTML5 and JavaScript apps and games as native mobile apps with accelerated canvas rendering.

entries.name: Cognitive computing
entries.definition: Computing systems that imitate aspects of human thinking, such as learning, reasoning and understanding language, using methods like machine learning and natural language processing.

entries.name: Cognitive load
entries.definition: The amount of mental effort being used in working memory at a given time, a concept used in teaching and interface design to avoid overloading people.

entries.name: Collaboration
entries.definition: Working jointly with others, sharing information and effort, to reach a shared goal.

entries.name: Collaboration software
entries.definition: Software that lets groups work together on shared tasks and documents, for example through shared files, chat and project boards.

entries.name: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment
entries.definition: A supply-chain practice in which trading partners jointly plan, forecast and replenish stock using shared data.

entries.name: Color matching
entries.definition: Choosing or adjusting colours so that a product or print matches a reference colour, as in paint, printing, textiles and cosmetics.
